learned.description: Next.js 15 ISR+Edge SSE frontend adopted from hive-frontend-proposal; deployed to Vercel via root vercel.json rootDirectory=web; GitHub status/ branch as data bus

For multi-output entities, skip_if_null must be checked in _transform_multi_output BEFORE the output loop, not inside _process_single_output. If the guard fires inside the loop, a required_fk null will throw TransformationError before the skip check is reached.
learned.example: router.py: if should_skip(record, config): return [] before for output_config in config['outputs']

learned.description: When consolidating multiple open PRs into a single release branch: (1) merge in dependency order; (2) 3-way merge auto-resolves disjoint changes — no manual intervention needed; (3) conflicts only arise when PRs insert different content at the same location; (4) close individual PRs as 'superseded by #N' after the release branch is opened.
learned.example: release/combined-fixes: PRs #34/#35/#36 → PR #37; users.py auto-merged cleanly

learned.description: build_soft_deleted_record() produces only __metadata__[soft_deleted]=True and skips all FK lookup resolution. Tests for inactive records (statecode=1) must NOT assert FK fields — they will not be present in the output.

New auth checks (API key, webhook HMAC) must read the env var at each call and return early (not raise) when unset. This is fail-open by design for gradual rollout — enforce by setting API_KEY / WEBHOOK_SECRET in production.
learned.example: security.py: if not _API_KEY: return; if not _WEBHOOK_SECRET: return

learned.description: Any transformer output that gates user access must have soft_delete:True. Without it, deactivating the Dataverse record (statecode=1) never reaches FAAST, leaving the user with persistent portal access indefinitely.

skip_if_null on a required_fk is a silent data-loss anti-pattern: it suppresses the entire output when the FK is null, leaving stale data in FAAST indefinitely. The correct fix is optional_fk with default=None, which emits null explicitly.
learned.example: PR #34: removed skip_if_null from P247_CONTACTACCESS_CONFIG; switched to optional_fk

learned.description: Use optional_fk(entity, field, default=None) to pass null FK values downstream as explicit None, enabling FAAST to clear stale foreign keys. Never use required_fk for nullable relationships — it throws TransformationError on null.
Kills stuck workers, refreshes shell state, and validates external dependencies before resuming operations.

SOLUTION: SQL injection risk through config-driven table/column name interpolation in lookup_resolver.py → Add _validate_sql_identifier(name, context) using allowlist regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_]+$. Call at all 3 interpolation sites (table name, column name, resolve_to_field). Raises ValueError for any non-matching identifier before it reaches the SQL query. Verified: PR #37 / commit e6ca5c2, test_validate_sql_identifier_*.

SOLUTION: User retains portal access after Dataverse contact access record is deactivated (ticket #29672) → Set soft_delete:True on the investment_profiles output of P247_CONTACTACCESS_CONFIG. This makes the transformer emit __metadata__['soft_deleted']=True when statecode=1, which triggers FAAST's RecordLoader.handleSoftDelete() to set deleted_at. Verified: PR #37 / commit ba840cd, test_inactive_contactaccess_soft_deletes_investment_profile.

SOLUTION: Null account FK causes TransformationError and stale investment_group_id in FAAST → Change _p247_account_value from required_fk to optional_fk('p247_account','investment_group_id'). Remove skip_if_null. This emits investment_group_id=None explicitly in the output data, which the FAAST SQS consumer can use to clear the stale FK. Verified: PR #37 / commit 62d8094, test_contactaccess_null_account_outputs_null_investment_group_id.

Noted gaps for future PRs: no replay/timestamp window, no weak-key length check, algorithm downgrade (sha1= prefix) not rejected.

We have a clear merge path and hardened capabilities to deploy, pending resource relief and final reviews.
orchestrator_sessions.progress: Merged PR #37 release/combined-fixes (rollup of #34/#35/#36), fixed research_loop infinite-synthesis, and validated all 34 hive self-tests including org_guard + HIVE_GITHUB_REPO propagation.
next_steps: Throttle/queue non-critical workers and raise low-priority nice values to drop core load below 1.0 and free memory headroom.
Resume research_loop with bounded concurrency and add circuit-breaker to halt synthesis on sustained load > 0.9 core.
Secure sign-off from Tim on PR #37 and merge release/combined-fixes → main; tag and promote to canary fleet.
Implement P4 bolder-transformer hardening (env-gated security rollout; optional-fk-null-passthrough for skip-if-null paths).
Deploy P8 FAAST SQS consumer update to backfill null investment_profiles rows and enable soft-delete access revocation.
decisions: Cap research_loop parallelism at 2 and auto-pause on load/core > 0.9 until 5m average < 0.7.
Merge PR #37 to main only after Tim’s review and canary promotion; rollback plan on first elevated-error spike.
Prioritize P8 SQS consumer and P4 transformer hardening over non-critical enhancements until load stabilizes.
